decisive_items: cervical spine deformity with scoliotic and kyphotic changes
demonstrating scoliotic and kyphotic changes in cervical spine
response.rationale: The clinical presentation of pronounced head and neck flexion and imaging confirming kyphotic changes in the cervical spine are most consistent with cervical kyphosis. Other candidates are either too broad (cervical spondylosis) or lack direct support (osteoporosis, DISH, scoliosis).

rejected.why: Osteoporosis is not directly supported; imaging shows structural deformity without mention of bone density or fractures.
DISH is not supported; no evidence of ossification or ligamentous changes.
Cervical scoliosis is less specific; the dominant deformity is flexion (kyphosis), not lateral curvature.
